questions.question: The value of θ, when: √3 cos θ + sin θ = 1, (1 ≤ θ ≤ 90°), is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of θ, when: √3 cos θ + sin θ = 1, (1 ≤ θ ≤ 90°), is:
questions.solution:
√3cosθ + sinθ = 1 ⇒ √3cosθ = 1 - sinθ ⇒ 3cos2θ = 1 + sin2θ - 2sinθ

⇒ 3 - 3sin2θ = 1 + sin2θ - 2sinθ ⇒ 2sin2θ - sinθ - 1 = 0

⇒ (2sinθ + 1)(sinθ - 1) = 0 ⇒ sinθ = 1 or -1/2 ⇒ θ = 90º

questions.question: Study the given bar-graph and answer the question that follows. What is the ratio of the number of countries with above-average numbers of engineers to the number of countries with below-average numbers of engineers?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given bar-graph and answer the question that follows.

What is the ratio of the number of countries with above-average numbers of engineers to the number of countries with below-average numbers of engineers?
questions.solution:
Total engineers = 20 + 55 + 25 + 65 + 85 + 90 = 340, Average = 340 / 6 ≈ 57

Above-average: USA (85), India (90) => 85 + 90 = 175

Below-average: Bhutan (20), Japan (55), Nepal (25), Australia (65) => 20 + 55 + 25 + 65 = 165

Ratio = 175 / 165 ≈ 1:1

questions.question: For what least value of n, 2 2n + 2n is completely divided by 6, where n is an integer?
questions.questionHtml: For what least value of n, 2<sup>2n</sup> + 2n is completely divided by 6, where n is an integer?
questions.solution:
22n + 2n is even (divisible by 2) ⇒ 22n mod 3 = (-1)n mod 3

⇒ 2n mod 3 = (-1)n mod 3 ⇒ 22n + 2n mod 3 = 2(-1)n = 0 mod 3

(-1)n = 0 when n = 1

questions.question: A trader offers the following discount schemes on the purchase of a refrigerator. ( i ) a discount of 10% followed by a discount of 8% ( ii ) successive discounts of 12% and 10% ( iii ) two successive discounts of 12% ( iv ) a discount of 20% In which scheme is the selling price the lowest?
questions.questionHtml:
A trader offers the following discount schemes on the purchase of a refrigerator.
( i ) a discount of 10% followed by a discount of 8%
( ii ) successive discounts of 12% and 10%
( iii ) two successive discounts of 12%
( iv ) a discount of 20%
In which scheme is the selling price the lowest?
questions.solution:
100 × (1 - 0.10) × (1 - 0.08) = 100 × 0.90 × 0.92 = 82.8

⇒ 100 × (1 - 0.12) × (1 - 0.10) = 100 × 0.88 × 0.90 = 79.2

⇒ 100 × (1 - 0.12)2 = 100 × 0.88 × 0.88 = 77.44

⇒ 100 × (1 - 0.20) = 100 × 0.80 = 80

questions.question: 10 years ago, the age of Sunita was thrice the age of her daughter Tanya. 10 years hence, the age of Sunita will be twice the age of Tanya. What is the ratio of their present ages?
questions.questionHtml: 10 years ago, the age of Sunita was thrice the age of her daughter Tanya. 10 years hence, the age of Sunita will be twice the age of Tanya. What is the ratio of their present ages?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of Sunita be S and the present age of Tanya be T.

S - 10 = 3(T - 10) ⇒ S + 10 = 2(T + 10) S = 3T - 20

⇒ S = 2T + 10 ⇒ 3T - 20 = 2T + 10 ⇒ T = 30 ⇒ S = 70

The ratio of their present ages: 70 : 30 ⇒ 7 : 3

questions.question: R targets to score 85% marks in exams. He scores 450 marks and misses the target by 35%. How much increment in percentage should be there in his scored marks to meet the target?
questions.questionHtml: R targets to score 85% marks in exams. He scores 450 marks and misses the target by 35%. How much increment in percentage should be there in his scored marks to meet the target?
questions.solution:
Let the total marks be M. Marks required = 0.85M

0.85M - 450 = 0.35M ⇒ 0.5M = 450 ⇒ M = 900

Required marks = 0.85 × 900 = 765

Increment = 765 - 450 = 315

Percentage increment = (315 / 450) × 100 = 70%

questions.question: Study the given table and answer the question that follows. The following table shows the production of printers by four plants of a company over the five years. What is the difference between the average production of plant 1 and plant 2 during five years?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given table and answer the question that follows.
The following table shows the production of printers by four plants of a company over the five years.

 
What is the difference between the average production of plant 1 and plant 2 during five years?
questions.solution:
Given:

Plant 1 Production (in thousands): 35, 43, 48, 32, 42

Plant 2 Production (in thousands): 25, 44, 39, 40, 44

Formula used:

Total Production = Sum of yearly production for each plant.

Average Production = Total Production / 5 (since there are 5 years).

Calculations:

For Plant 1:

Total Production = 35,000 + 43,000 + 48,000 + 32,000 + 42,000 = 200,000

Average Production = 200,000 / 5 = 40,000

For Plant 2:

Total Production = 25,000 + 44,000 + 39,000 + 40,000 + 44,000 = 192,000

Average Production = 192,000 / 5 = 38,400

Difference between averages:

40,000 - 38,400 = 1,600

Conclusion:

The difference between the average production of Plant 1 and Plant 2 during the five years is 1,600 (in thousands).

questions.question: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 4 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. At 8:00 a.m., pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B is opened at 9:00 a.m.?
questions.questionHtml: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 4 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. At 8:00 a.m., pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B is opened at 9:00 a.m.?
questions.solution:
Work done by A in 1 hour = 1/4

Combined work done by A and B in 1 hour = 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12

Remaining work after 9:00 a.m. = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4

Time to complete remaining work = (3/4) / (5/12) = 9/5 hours = 1.8 hours

1.8 hours = 1 hour and 48 minutes

Tank will be filled at 9:00 a.m. + 1 hour 48 minutes = 10:48 a.m.

questions.question: Let x = r cos (t), y = r sin (t) cos (u), z = r sin (t)sin (u). Then the value of x 2 + y 2 + z 2 is ___.
questions.questionHtml: Let x = r cos (t), y = r sin (t) cos (u), z = r sin (t)sin (u). Then the value of x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> is ___.
questions.solution:
x = r cos(t), y = r sin(t) cos(u), z = r sin(t) sin(u)

⇒ x2 + y2 + z2 = (r cos(t))2 + (r sin(t) cos(u))2 + (r sin(t) sin(u))2

⇒ r2 cos2(t) + r2 sin2(t) cos2(u) + r2 sin2(t) sin2(u)

⇒ r2 (cos2(t) + sin2(t)(cos2(u) + sin2(u)))

⇒ r2 (cos2(t) + sin2(t)) = r2

questions.question: Simplify. \(\frac{(232)^3+(140)^3+(353)^3-3\times232\times140\times353}{(232)^2+(140)^2+(353)^2-232\times140-140\times353-353\times232}\)
questions.solution:
Using identity: a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - bc - ca)

\(\dfrac{(232 +140+353)((232)^2+(140)^2+(353)^2-232×140-140×353-353×232)}{(232)^2+(140)^2+(353)^2-232×140-140×353-353×232}\)

⇒ (232 + 140 + 353) = 725

questions.question: Aman has certain number of notes of denomination ₹20 and ₹10 which amount to ₹390. If the numbers of notes of each kind are interchanged, then the new amount is ₹90 less than before. Find the number of notes of ₹20 denomination.
questions.questionHtml: Aman has certain number of notes of denomination ₹20 and ₹10 which amount to ₹390. If the numbers of notes of each kind are interchanged, then the new amount is ₹90 less than before. Find the number of notes of ₹20 denomination.
questions.solution:
20x + 10y = 390  ............(i)

20y + 10x = 300  ............(ii)

Multiply (ii) by 2:

40y + 20x = 600.  ............(iii)

Subtract (i) from (iii):

40y + 20x - 20x - 10y = 210 ⇒ 30y = 210 ⇒ y = 7

Substitute y in (i):

20x + 70 = 390 ⇒ 20x = 320 ⇒ x = 16

questions.question: If 4tanθ - 3 = 0, then the value of \(\frac{1 - cos2θ}{1 + cos2θ}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If 4tanθ - 3 = 0, then the value of \(\frac{1 - cos2θ}{1 + cos2θ}\) is:
questions.solution:
4tanθ - 3 = 0 ⇒ tanθ = 3/4 ⇒ tan2θ = (1 - cos2θ) / (1 + cos2θ)

⇒ (3/4)2 = (1 - cos2θ) / (1 + cos2θ) ⇒ (1 - cos2θ) / (1 + cos2θ) = 9/16

questions.question: A triangle ABC is made on a circle, where AB is diameter of the circle. If BC is equal to the radius of the circle and ∠ABC = x ∠BAC, then x is :
questions.questionHtml: A triangle ABC is made on a circle, where AB is diameter of the circle. If BC is equal to the radius of the circle and ∠ABC = x ∠BAC, then x is :
questions.solution:
Let ∠BAC = θ, ∠ABC = xθ. Since ∠ACB = 90° 

⇒ θ + xθ + 90° = 180°, θ(1 + x) = 90°, θ = 90° / (1 + x)

⇒ AB = 2r ⇒ sin(θ) = r / 2r = 1 / 2 ⇒ θ = 30°

⇒ 30° = 90° / (1 + x) ⇒ 1 + x = 3 ⇒ x = 2

questions.question: The bar graph shows the number of students present in a class on four days. The average number of students present on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday is:
questions.questionHtml: The bar graph shows the number of students present in a class on four days. The average number of students present on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Number of students present on Monday = 25

Number of students present on Tuesday = 30

Number of students present on Wednesday = 20

Formula Used:

Average number of students present = Total number of students / Number of days

Calculations:

Total number of students present = 25 + 30 + 20 = 75

⇒ Average number of students present = 75 / 3 = 25

The average number of students present on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday is 25.

questions.question: Amit and Bilal buy goods for ₹1,500 and ₹2,000, respectively. Amit marks his goods up by y%, while Bilal marks his goods up by 2y% and offers a discount of y%. If both make the same profit, then find the value of y.
questions.questionHtml: Amit and Bilal buy goods for ₹1,500 and ₹2,000, respectively. Amit marks his goods up by y%, while Bilal marks his goods up by 2y% and offers a discount of y%. If both make the same profit, then find the value of y.
questions.solution:
Amit's SP = 1500 + 15y, Profit = 15y

Bilal's SP = (2000 + 40y) - (20y + 0.4y2) = 2000 + 20y - 0.4y2, Profit = 20y - 0.4y2

Equate profits: 15y = 20y - 0.4y2 ⇒ 0.4y2 = 5y ⇒ y(y - 12.5) = 0

⇒ y = 12.5
